The aulos is an aerophone of ancient Greece, Hornbostel–Sachs number 422.111.2, used in the cult of Dionysos, in sacrifice, drama, military music and athletic contests, as an accompaniment to elegiac verse, and to mark the stroke on a trireme. In modern revivals it has joined the line-up of the Lost Sounds Orchestra and appears in the films Agora and 300; the composer Ludwig Göransson used replica instruments in his score for the 2026 film The Odyssey. There is also the Bosios nomos, a piece written for solo aulos and performed at the Apollonian games in 582 BC.
阿夫洛斯管為氣鳴樂器，常見形式以雙管、雙簧發聲。演奏者使用面頰帶：一條置於頭頂，: The aulos is an aerophone, and in its common form it sounds with two pipes and double reeds. The player uses a cheek strap: one band over the top of the head and another drawn from ear to ear behind the head, to support the cheeks, steady the instrument, and help with circular breathing and sustained blowing. For a beginner the point is to take the mouthpiece into the mouth so that the reeds vibrate, to hold the lip position so that the lip muscles are not overworked, and to control the amount of air so as not to overblow.
阿夫洛斯管由蘆葦、竹或木材製成雙管結構，主要使用無節蘆葦或竹子製作發聲管體。管身: The aulos is built as a double pipe of reed, bamboo or wood, with the sounding tubes made mainly from jointless reed or bamboo. The body can be worked from hardwoods such as paulownia or birch for greater durability. The two pipes carry adjustable cane reeds, tied in place with animal membrane or plant fibre. The end of the pipe may be decorated with bone or ivory, and some finer instruments use metal ferrules to strengthen the joint. Fingerholes are bored along the body, and the pitch is usually adjusted with plugs of stone, ivory or metal. The whole design is light and portable, so that a player can carry it through every kind of ceremony.
阿夫洛斯管見於古希臘與地中海考古和圖像，神話將起源歸於雅典娜或瑪耳緒阿斯。它常見: The aulos is known from archaeology and images across ancient Greece and the Mediterranean, and myth traces its origin to Athena or to Marsyas. It is common in Dionysiac cult, sacrifice, drama, contests and military music; at the Apollonian games of 582 BC the Bosios nomos, written for solo aulos, was performed. It developed single-pipe, side-blown and bagpipe types. From the late fifth century it passed from amateur aristocratic practice to professional musicians, often slaves. Thebes, Sparta and Athens judged it differently; Sparta used it to accompany the hoplites on the march.
阿夫洛斯管音色嘹亮刺激，具有強烈的穿透力，音質帶有明亮而略帶尖銳的特徵。其音域寬: The aulos is loud and exciting, with strong carrying power and a tone that is bright and slightly sharp at the edge. Its range is wide, covering everything from low to high, and it is especially good at raised, excited utterance. The instrument resonates mainly through the vibration of the air inside the body, and the twin pipes let it produce harmonic effects that add fullness. Compared with the ancient flute, the aulos is rougher and more forceful; compared with stringed instruments such as the harp, its tone is more aggressive and more dramatic. These qualities give it great force in religious ritual and revel, and help to build an atmosphere of ecstasy and intoxication.
